answer: A vault-backed stake bond resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a meaningful, time-delayed deposit in a shared vault before it can earn or attest, like a pearl held as collateral rather than a free username. Creating one identity is cheap, but creating thousands means locking thousands of deposits that cannot be withdrawn quickly, so a saffron-marked reputation built slowly is lost if the agent cheats. An attacker must therefore pay real, illiquid capital per fake identity, while honest agents reuse one bond across many honest actions.
